note: A dossier is every mention of a person anywhere in this archive, gathered automatically after the site is built and linked back to the page it appears on. Identity here is by NAME, not by resolved individual — where two people share a name they share this page, and the archive says so rather than guessing. Nothing on a dossier page is new evidence; it is the same evidence, brought together.

gerthardus-lodewikus-booysen.r: THE ONE DOCUMENT THAT NAMES HIM HAS BEEN WEAKENED, AND BY SOMEBODY WHO HAD NOT SEEN IT. On 14 September 2026 PIETER VAN ZYL, answering this archive’s G2G question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household — and added, from memory, that he thought a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus was called Gerhardus Lodewicus. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE CHILD IS ON THE SAME SHEET: line 12 of that very notice names JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN among the eight children. So the name this archive takes from LINE 3, for the dead man’s FATHER, is the back half of his SON’S name, eight lines below, in one clerk’s hand — and the half that is dropped, JAN, is the name de Villiers gives as the real father. THIS DOES NOT PROVE THE FATHER WAS JAN and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. It removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. The top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. He still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The atlas → What is still missing Thirteen questions , several answered and one closed — and the oldest still open. Who Gerthardus Lodewikus Booysen's parents were; whether the County Cork the family speaks of is real at all. Three enquiries are out and unanswered: the Western Cape Archives, the National Archives in Pretoria, and the SANDF Documentation Centre, which has delivered half of what was asked. The list, and what would close each one, is at Open questions . Nothing here is taken on trust because it appears in a family tree.

petrus-jacobus-booysen.r: Married at about seventeen; died a widower in the Transvaal, eighty-eight years old, on a farm called Brakfontein. His Sterfkennis — No. 678, written 14 September 1876 — is the oldest document about this family that this archive has read, it names his parents, and it lists eight children. Estate: NOTHING. “Niets nagelaten. Niets bekend.”

also.r: Farmer at Zevenfontein, Brak River. Signed his wife's 1863 death notice. Died fifteen years before the war.

david-schalk-booijsen.r: First on his father's 1876 death notice, and a major — and now with a date. His baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names his parents as PIETER JACOBUS BOOIJZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE, which is the only document in this archive that puts Anna Maria in the family at all. His father was eighteen when he was born. He married ADRIANA CHRISTINA VILJOEN — on 3 NOVEMBER 1828 AT CRADOCK, a date and a place this archive did not have until WikiTree was read on 13 September 2026, and FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ — and named a daughter ANNA MARIA in 1835, after his own mother. His nephew, born 1848, carries the same name — the two are told apart only by a generation.

jan-gerthardus-lodewikus-booijsen.r: Fifth on his father’s 1876 notice, and named for the man at the top of the line. HIS is the estate TAB MHG O/2899, which this archive had spent months attributing to his nephew of the same name born in 1855 — the Transvaal probate index gives him as the deceased, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria died on the same farm in 1920, and her death notice names him. He is how this family reaches the western Transvaal.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The date had no source except the file number. The Transvaal probate index names the estate's deceased in full: Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg — born about 1818, which is his UNCLE, fifth on the 1876 Sterfkennis. The nephew's death date is withdrawn and nothing is known about what became of him. The particular error is worth naming: the archive read a year off a reference number, wrote it in as a fact, and then cited the fact back.

magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.n: Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg
magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.r: His daughter, and the first person in the western Transvaal this archive can attach to the line rather than merely set beside it. Her 1920 Sterfkennis — estate 44420, stamped Pretoria 16 August 1920 — names her parents as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen and Magdalena Susanna Maria, gives her age as 59 years 9 months, and lists seven children. Her son-in-law B. J. van den Berg signed it.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Lichtenburg joins the line · Found The same correction does the opposite favour. Vaalbank, in the district of Lichtenburg, is where the 1876 man's son died in 1885 — and this archive had already read a 1920 Sterfkennis from that farm for Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen about 1860, father entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen, filed under “NOT PROVED”. She is his daughter. Two deaths on one farm thirty-five years apart, which is settlement rather than passage. Read west along the atlas: Rustenburg 1876, Lichtenburg 1885 and 1920, Marico 1903.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The direct ancestor died in district Rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before Johannesburg. Two other notices read the same afternoon sit in the same country: a Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen , who died at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg in 1920 and whose father is entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen ; and an an Anna Johanna Booijzen , born in the district of Cradock about 1823, who died on a farm in the district of Rustenburg in 1891, leaving children called Petrus Jacobus, Magdalena Johanna and Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas.

charlotta-elizabetha-dormehl.r: His second wife, married at Zeerust on 14 April 1892 when she was fifty-one and he sixty-three, and her own Death Notice 844 gives the rest: born Graaff-Reinet about October 1841, FARMER'S WIFE, father JACOB DORMEHL and mother UNKNOWN, dead at Driefontein in Groot Marico on 6 February 1902 aged 60 years 4 months, leaving ONE WAGON AND HOUSEHOLD FURNITURE worth £51 8s 0d and a will. THREE HUSBANDS — Jacob van Staden, then Matthys Roos, then Booysen — and SIX CHILDREN, two van Stadens and four Rooses, NOT ONE OF THEM A BOOYSEN. That is why the four children this archive once drew under her are not hers.

And after ten years of marriage to Hendrik Stefanus Booysen, no child of his is named , because she was fifty-one when she married him. This archive spent a month drawing his four children under her. Earlier today the 1892 marriage register — her age, her condition — made that impossible. Her own death notice now says the same thing from the other side, in her husband’s handwriting.

diederik-arnoldus-booysen.r: A KARWEIER — a transport rider — of Zwartruggens, and a son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elizabeth Johanna Sophia Myburgh. His Sterfkennis 87882 is the first document in this archive printed in Afrikaans rather than Dutch or English, and the first Booysen estate here worth more than £300. He married Elizabeth Anna Bronkhorst, widow Joubert, in community of property; their youngest son carries his grandfather’s name.

anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.v: Anna Johanna Booijzen, gebooren Oliefier (1891) · Anna Catrena (1891) · born Olivier (1908)
anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.r: THE FIRST WIFE OF HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJSEN, and for a week this archive had her filed as a stranger. Her own Sterfkennis 6332 gives her parents as OCKEN JOHANNES OLIEFIER and ANNA JOHANNA BOTHA, her age as 67 years 8 months and 1 day, her farm as BRAKFONTEIN — which this archive read as Boekfontein — and her surname as OLIEFIER, which this archive read as Alberts. She was still married when she died: her husband outlived her by seventeen years and remarried at Zeerust eleven months later. Seven children, all of age: Petrus Jacobus, Ocken Johannes, Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya, Alettha Catrina Johanna, Magdalena Johanna, Hendrick Stefanus Nicolaas. Her father is where OCKERT JOHANNES came into this family — and her 1824 baptism gives his name entire, OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER, which is exactly what her son was called. She married Hendrik Stephanus Booijzen at POTCHEFSTROOM on 3 JULY 1850, entry 206, she 25 and he 23 — the earliest evidence this archive has of this family north of the Vaal, twenty-six years before the 1876 death at Rustenburg and two years before the Sand River Convention.

hits.text: Both are the right names in the right district at the right time, and this archive could no longer say what it had been saying. What was withdrawn → Since then the second of those two has been settled. The farm is Brakfontein , not Boekfontein, and the maiden name is Oliefier , not Alberts. She is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , the first wife of Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen, and she died on the family's own farm. How that was read → 1937–38 · A whole estate, from the death to the last shilling Estates 58379 and 58380 , KAB MOOC 6/9/5047 — on this archive's Sources page as "Located, not yet read" for months. Read now, and not just the death notices: the liquidation account and the distribution account too.

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: It comes in with one wife, from the district of Cradock, and then will not leave. Who When What they are to the name Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier m. 1816 HER FATHER. Married Anna Catharina Botha at Graaff-Reinet on 8 December 1816 and baptised four children at Cradock. Not a Booysen. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier the younger b. Feb 1826 His son, named for him entire. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen 15 Sep 1852 – 16 Jan 1921 HIS GRANDSON, by Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier — and the man who signed his own father's death notice in 1908. Confirmed at Rustenburg in 1869 on the same Sunday as his brother. Ockert Johannes Stefanus Booysen of 1894 b. 16 May 1894 Baptised at Rustenburg, a great-nephew.

hits.text: Her name is the one that then travels: an ANGELINE KOLBE dies at Wakkerstroom in 1900 and a MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE is buried at Volksrust in 1901, aged two months. Neither can yet be attached to her, and this archive will not guess.

anna-maria-van-der-merwe.r: WikiTree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW—which, if right, is where the forename DAVID SCHALK entered this family: her eldest son carries her father’s names entire.FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and it is checkable against the van der Merwe baptism registers rather than the tree. His wife, married 1805 at Graaff-Reinet — and DOCUMENTED, which she was not until today. A Dutch Reformed baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names her as the mother of DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 December 1806, who is FIRST of the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis. That resolves a contradiction this archive marked Serious (they were married by 1806, so the 1825 Cape Town marriage record is a different couple) and it rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said only a family tree put her there. WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED is that she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line.

hits.text: But “Serious”, not resolved — two men of one name in one town is precisely the mistake this archive keeps catching itself in, and the 1940 notice still names nobody. The inferred row stands, flagged, until a document settles it. → Anna Maria van der Merwe — married 1805 or 1825? The tree marries her to Petrus Jacobus Booysen in 1805 at Graaff-Reinet and has her dead “before March 1825”. FamilySearch carries a Dutch Reformed marriage of PETRUS JACOBUS BOOŸZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE dated 9 MARCH 1825, at Cape Town, indexed three separate times. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Mother and daughter under the same two forenames — and the daughter who died a minor makes three. Lady Grey, which this archive already knows “Lady Grey, near Aliwal North, Cape Colony.” That is the family’s own church. Willem Hermanus “William Henry” Booyzen married Catherine Maria Sophia “Kathleen” Barry at Lady Grey on 22 December 1879. And David Schalk Booysen, born 9 June 1848, is his brother — fourth on the 1863 death notice of their mother Johanna Catharina Mountjoy, where Willem Hermanus is sixth. Two brothers married out of one small Cape church; one went east to the coal at Indwe and died there in 1905, the other went north to Pretoria.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The women are not. Mountjoy (1838). Barry (1879). Kinnear (1940s). Behind the Barrys, Kolbe — a German tailor's family out of Soho who sailed as 1820 Settlers and named a Karoo farm Wurtemburg . Behind the Kolbes, Downing . That is why David Defranceski's great-grandfather, born on a farm in the Eastern Cape in 1901, was christened George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen . Every one of those forenames is a woman's surname. The women → And it is why the tree folds back on itself: in 1924 George married his own first cousin once removed , so his daughter Catherine descends from one Barry–Kolbe couple twice over. The cousin marriage → Corrections are the most valuable thing anyone can send.

hits.text: Resolved RESOLVED. His 1845 death notice (estate 7698) and his gravestone both give 1 December 1844, and neither his notice nor his widow’s 1867 notice lists a Julia. Reject the child, keep the date. The same two documents also drop KEETOR PETER BENJAMIN KOLBE, whom the tree gives a 1840 birth — he is in neither list. → George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen (1901–1947) Death dated 21 February 1947, with burial ten months later on 14 December 1947. Resolved RESOLVED by his death notice: he died 11 December 1947 and was buried on the 14th. “21 February” is the date the notice was signed — in 1948. "The day of the decease: On 11th December 1947 " — died at 85 Rheeden St, Forest Hill , Johannesburg. He died on 11 December 1947 — not 21 February 1947. 21 February is the date the notice was signed , and it was signed in 1948 . A transcriber conflated the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1915 death notice shows she is the same woman as Kathleen above. Withdrawn. Read rows five and seven together. Catherina Maria Sophia Barry died on 30 July 1859. Catherine Maria Sophia Barry was born on 4 August 1859 — five days later , and was given the dead child's name. That name then travelled: to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1891–1946) , and to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) , David Defranceski's grandmother. A four-year-old's death in Burgersdorp is still being commemorated, unknowingly, four generations later.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts. Where a person five generations back should have thirty-two separate ancestors, she has thirty — because one couple occupies two of the slots.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden. And a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known.

david-schalk-booysen.r: PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 54 against a birth of 9 June 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. If it is him, he was a Transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back — he remarried at Pretoria in November 1905. Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.
p: A zinc building in Market Street

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: 1900 · A zinc building in Market Street, Pretoria — and the direct line’s own brother A run of ten index entries under Booijzen in the Transvaal probate records carried no dates, no places and nothing to identify them. They all belong to one death notice , and it opens a household this archive did not have: the family of David Schalk Booysen , born 9 June 1848 — the brother of the direct ancestor . Death Notice 4795 , filed 18 March 1904 and stamped by the Master of the Supreme Court, Transvaal, on 2 May 1904 — nearly four years after the death . hits.title: Charles Petrus Barend Lowies
hits.text: Born in the district of CRADOCK about 1849, within a year of David Schalk Booysen and in the same Karoo district; dead at Pretoria, where David Schalk had been widowed five years earlier. His parents were JAN LOWIES and ELISABETHA MARIA LUBBE, and he left TWELVE children. THE FILE IS NOW READ. He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place.

johanna-elena-stols.r: His second wife, married at Pretoria on 27 November 1905 — she 51 and a WIDOW LOWIES of Skinners Court, he 56 and a widower of Goede Hoop. Her first husband was CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES, born in the district of Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria on 5 JUNE 1905 — FIVE MONTHS AND TWENTY-TWO DAYS before she married again. Estate 7081, which the marriage register cites beside his 4795. TWELVE children by Lowies, SIX OF THEM STILL MINORS when he died — and her second husband lived at the same address, GOEDEHOOP. She signed her first husband’s death notice on 27 October 1905 and married her second on 27 November.

charles-petrus-barend-lowies.r: Her first husband, and estate 7081 — the OTHER number cited in the Remarks column of the 1905 marriage register. Born in the district of CRADOCK about 1849, within a year of David Schalk Booysen and in the same Karoo district; dead at Pretoria, where David Schalk had been widowed five years earlier. His parents were JAN LOWIES and ELISABETHA MARIA LUBBE, and he left TWELVE children. THE FILE IS NOW READ. He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place. Dutch, of the Cradock district, 56 years and 8 months, dead in the LUNATIC ASYLUM at Pretoria on 5 June 1905. Movables but no land, an estate over £100, and a will. Six of the twelve children were still minors. His widow signed the notice on 27 October and married David Schalk on 27 November.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow. The Master cleared both estates within four days: 4795 on 4 November, 7081 on the 7th, the wedding on the 27th.

hits.text: 4795 was David Schalk’s and led back to his first wife’s death notice. This is 7081 , read entire — and it is not the document this archive expected. hits.title: What changed
hits.text: 4795 was the groom's and led back to his first wife's death notice. 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow.

Nothing movable left, and a compensation claim filed.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart. Five of the eight children of that marriage are named for a parent or a grandparent — the same habit as the Barry names crossing into the Daschners, seen from the other direction and in another family. Johanna Catharina Booysen gets her dates · Found Second on the 1863 death notice and until now nothing but a position in a list. The Dutch Reformed index gives her born 15 May 1844 and baptised at BRAK RIVIER on 4 August 1844 — the farm her father was still on nineteen years later when her mother died there. A small thing, and the kind the register was built to hand over.

gerrit-jacobus-booysen.d: Aug 1951, Middelburg — the day illegible on the stone
gerrit-jacobus-booysen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it says more than its index line. “IN DANKBARE HULDE AAN ONS GELIEFDE VADER EN OUPA — GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN — GEB. 19 JAN. 1870 — OORL. 2_ AUG. 1951 — SY GENADE WAS VIR MY GENOEG.” THE BIRTH DAY MATCHES THIS ARCHIVE EXACTLY, and from a source that is not the death notice it came from: 19 January 1870, cut in granite. THE DEATH IS NOW A MONTH instead of a year — AUGUST 1951 — and the day is a 2 followed by a digit this archive cannot read off the photograph, so it is not guessed. VADER EN OUPA: he was a grandfather, which no document here had said. AND THE LAST LINE IS IN THE FIRST PERSON — “His grace was enough for ME” — a widower’s sentence, cut twenty-one years after his wife died. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED. The eGGSA gravestone library holds “BOOYZEN GERT JACOBUS 1870-1951” in the MIDDELBURG MAIN CEMETERY, Eastern Cape — born 1870 and dead in 1951, which is the year of estate TAB MHG 5155/51, the file this archive has been trying to read on blocked film. He is buried a few stones from his wife. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. The only child entered on his father's 1884 death notice, and born seven years after the first wife died — so a child of the second marriage. He married Isabella Frederika Coetsee at Middelburg on 23 March 1896, and his own son was baptised BOOYZEN, with a z, in 1904.

COETSEE) — GEB. 15 APRIL 1874 — OORL. 31 MAART 1930 — HEMELSE RUS.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE. This archive had “c. May 1874”, worked back from an age; the stone gives 15 APRIL 1874, and an exact date cut on a stone beats a month inferred from an age. THE DEATH MATCHES TO THE DAY — 31 March 1930 — which is a third independent source saying 1930 and not 1943. AND HER GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN ISABELLA FREDERICKA NEE COETSEE 1874-1930”, Middelburg main cemetery, in the eGGSA library. The stone's dates match her own death notice exactly and CONFIRM THE CORRECTION below from a second, independent source — the stone says 1930, not 1943. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. Married Gerrit Jacobus at Middelburg, 23 March 1896. THIS ARCHIVE HAD HER DYING IN 1943 AND HAS TAKEN IT BACK: 1943 is when her husband finally filed, thirteen years after the death. johanna-booyzen.r: NOT THIS FAMILY, and recorded here on purpose. Death notice 6167 — the oldest Booyzen estate paper in the Cape Master's series, and a generation older in form than anything else this archive has read. Widow of Charles du Plessis; one daughter, married to Benjamin Solomon; “no property whatever except a Bond amounting per balance to £15”. Line 3 answers “both dead”. She is here because she was born in 1754 and died in 1843 — the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, both off the family tree with no source stated — and because somebody will one day find her and decide she is the same woman. She is not. Her name is not Magdelena, not Elisabeth, and not de Beer.

petrus-jacobus-booyzen.r: HIS STONE IS READ AND IT CONFIRMS BOTH DATES EXACTLY: “HIER RUS — MY GELIEFDE SEUN — PIETER J. BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Dead at thirty-two. AND ONE WORD OF IT DOES REAL WORK: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS”. A stone cut by ONE surviving parent — and his mother Isabella Frederika had been dead seven years when he died, so the parent is his father, GERT JACOBUS, who then lay down beside them both fourteen years later. Three of one household in one cemetery, and the grammar of the inscriptions gives the order they went in. Baptised in the Dutch Reformed register with a Z, son of Gert Jacobus Booyzen and Isabella Frederika Coetzee — the second marriage's line, at Middelburg, spelled Booyzen a year before the Indwe sheet.

hits.text: His widow wrote “oorlede” for both parents. Four death notices in this family now ask who the parents were, and four fail. He was a MESSELAAR, a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. The second wife, named — Johanna Margaritha Pretorius · Found The oldest open question in the archive, answered by a christening rather than a death. Every attempt had gone at death notices, which either do not ask for a wife's name or got “oorlede” for an answer.

Magdalena Johanna Francina Booijzen , born 16 July 1853. Both are on the 1863 death notice — the third and sixth of Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's eight children. Two children of the first marriage stood godparent to the first child of the second. Whatever the household was after 1863, it was not divided.

willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.d: 29 Jul 1932, Johannesburg Hospital — buried Brixton, grave 6889
willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.r: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. Husband and wife in one grave.

Susanna Adriana Roodt is the sixteen-year-old he married at Indwe on 21 September 1908. Husband and wife in one grave, thirty-six years apart. And the clerk spells him BOYSEN — the same spelling an English clerk used for a different man of this family on John Barry's 1915 death notice.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: MIJNWERKER — an eighth child, and the last line of the testimony · Found Four documents from the Dutch Reformed congregation at Indwe, found by typing “Indwe” into the register that was built yesterday. A Willem Hermanus BOOIJZEN, aged 21, is confirmed there on 31 May 1907, in a class that also holds Catharina Maria Elizabeth Roodt, 17, and Susanna Adriana Roodt, 15. On 21 September 1908 he marries Susanna Adriana Roodt, sixteen, at Indwe — certificate 13, her parents consenting — and under Rang of Beroep the register writes MIJNWERKER, of DUGMORE MIJN.

hits.text: Geref. Kerk at Indwe. Signed W. H. Booyzen and S. A. Roodt , before D. N. Claase and C. J. Slabbert , and checked against the original register by J. J. Knight . Their son was already four months old. Willem Hermanus Booyzen of Dugmore was born on 31 May 1908 and baptised at Indwe on 6 December 1908 — born before the wedding, baptised after it. The order of those three dates is the whole story of a twenty-two-year-old miner and a sixteen-year-old who needed her parents' consent, living on the same mine. john-barry-booyzen.r: HIS GRAVE IS READ, and it gives both dates at once. BRENTHURST CEMETERY, BRAKPAN: “IN LIEFDE HERINNERING — AAN ONS VADER — JOHN BARRY BOOYZEN — ★ 26.4.1884 — † 23.1.1952 — RUS SAG.”, cut by Pretoria Grafstene. This archive had “c. 1884” and NO DEATH AT ALL. It now has 26 APRIL 1884 and 23 JANUARY 1952 — the latter matching estate TAB MHG 769/52, a file still unread on a blocked film. “Aan ons vader”: he left children. AND NOW HE HAS A DEATH AND A PLACE. “BOOYZEN JOHN BARRY 1884-1952”, BRENTHURST CEMETERY, BRAKPAN. This archive had him as “c. 1884” with no death at all, and an estate number — TAB MHG 769/52 — on a film that will not open. The stone gives 1884-1952, which matches both the estimate and the estate year, and puts him on the East Rand rather than in Johannesburg. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. Eldest son. Present at his father's death in 1905 and the informant — he signs Booyzen four lines under the clerk's Booysen.

henry-james-booyzen.d: 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1
henry-james-booyzen.r: AND NOW THERE IS A REGISTER. The G2G question this archive posted on 13 September was answered within eighteen hours by PIETER VAN ZYL, who put the baptism on the profile: “South Africa, Dutch Reformed Church Registers (Cape Town Archives)”, ark 1:1:6KPT-T3Z4 — HENRY JAMES BOOŸSEN, BORN 12 AUGUST 1887, BAPTISED 27 NOVEMBER 1887, parents WILLEM HERMANUS BOOŸSEN and CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA BARRY. Verified here against the index directly. The 12 August 1887 has now travelled from a family tree, to a gravestone, to a church register, in that order, which is the wrong way round and is how it usually goes. THE SAME ANSWER ALSO SAYS he was A CARPENTER WHEN HE MARRIED and A RETIRED MINER OF LANGLAAGTE ESTATES when he died, OF PHTHISIS — and this archive has CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS off the Johannesburg burial register. Phthisis is the Rand miner’s disease and a retired Langlaagte miner dying of it in 1956 is entirely of a piece; but the two causes are not the same word and this archive has read only one of the two documents. REPORTED ON G2G, NOT VERIFIED HERE. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE BIRTH. WEST PARK, Johannesburg: “HIER RUS — MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT — HENRY JAMES — GEB. 12.8.1887 — OORL. 8.12.1956 — RUS IN VREDE”, over the surname BOOYZEN. The 12 August 1887 this archive carried marked FROM WIKITREE AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT is now on his own gravestone, and the death matches the burial register to the day. “My dierbare eggenoot” — the stone was raised by his widow, Dorothea Regina. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN HENRY JAMES 1887-1956”, WEST PARK CEMETERY, Johannesburg — matching the burial register this archive read and the 12 August 1887 birth WikiTree gives. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. WikiTree gives his birth as 12 AUGUST 1887 and his marriage as 17 JUNE 1912 AT ELLIOT, neither of which this archive had—bothFROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the “c. 1887” below is this archive’s own figure, worked back from an age on a burial register. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

richard-peter-booyzen.d: 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119
richard-peter-booyzen.r: TWENTY-FOUR, MARRIED, a SAWYER of 18 Anderson Street, Turffontein — dead of INFLUENZA AND PNEUMONIA after eleven days on 25 October 1918, the centre of Black October, and buried at Brixton on the 27th. Not in this archive before today. Added as a ninth child of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry on three grounds and no document: RICHARD PETER is her own brother's name; a birth about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901; and his registration gives his birthplace as the CAPE OF GOOD HOPE, which is the migration every one of her children made. A Transvaal death registration names no parents, so this stays INFERRED. And he was NOT A SOLDIER — which kills the best explanation this archive had for his mother's military pension.

hits.text: And two infants at Brixton the archive did not have at all. THEN OCTOBER 1918. RICHARD PETER BOOYZEN, twenty-four, buried at Brixton on the 27th — the centre of Black October. This archive has no Richard Peter Booyzen and it should: Richard Peter Barry is Kathleen's own brother, and a boy born about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901. Added as a ninth child, marked INFERRED, because a burial register names no parents. Two more Booysens went into the same ground within eight weeks and neither can be shown to be kin.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Born Cape Province. Indwe. Married. Since 1908. Forty-seven in July 1932 against twenty-two in September 1908 — which makes him forty-six. One year. Brixton Cemetery, 31 July 1932 , where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its Johannesburg dead: Anna J. Mary Booyzen in 1914, John Barry Booyzen in 1916, George Downing Daschner in 1925. And “Sasanna Adriana Booyzen” was buried at Johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him. What does not No parents are named , because a South African civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten.

catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.d: 1946 — West Park, grave 51, beside her husband
catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.r: Baptised at Barkly Oost 24 May 1891, entry 120, named for her mother entire, and fourteen when her father died at Indwe. She married Joseph Heinrich Daschner AT INDWE — the same village — and his 1942 death notice names her “born Booyzen”, with a z, in a Johannesburg typist’s hands. Eleven children, five of them carrying Booyzen and Barry forenames. She died in the Transvaal in 1946 — estate TAB MHG 3734/46, found only when this archive finally searched outside the Cape, and still to be read.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: It does not prove the rebel is Kathleen's brother. It does show that whoever named this child was standing inside the same family this archive is describing. The namesakes → How far the Barry names travel There is no Barry surname left in this family after 1859. There is a great deal of Barry name . The children of Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen — Kathleen Barry's daughter — on her husband's 1942 death notice. Kathleen Barry married a Booyzen in the 1880s, so the surname stops with her. Her daughter married a Daschner, so it is two surnames gone in two generations.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: And a DOUBLE PLOT: Joseph Heinrich Daschner, 58, buried 21 April 1942 in GRAVE 50 of a pair 50/51 he bought himself, with a memorial by L. Canata & Son — and the consecutive grave-number register braces 50 and 51 together, DASCHNER JOSEPH H. and DASCHNER CATHERINE M.S. She is Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen, born 22 April 1891 at Barkly Oost, George's own sister, whose estate MHG 3734/46 is one of the six files in the letter to Pretoria. Four years after he was buried in the first grave she went into the second.

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: Eleven years before the first Catherine Maria Sophia was born. Catherine Maria Sophia “Kathleen” Barry 1859–1940 The last Barry of the surname in this line. She married a Booyzen in 1879. Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen 1891–1946 Baptised at Barkly Oost, “named for her mother entire”. She married a Daschner at Indwe. Catherine Mary Sophia Daschner a major by 1942 Her eldest daughter — the third of the name, and the second surname it has crossed. Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen 1929–2013 And back into the Booyzens, on the direct line, the hinge to the Lerena archive. A fifth carries it too: Catharina Mary Sophia Däschner, born at Indwe on 11 March 1909, baptised there that May.

The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three columns. Buried 20 June 1925, D.R. section, grave 4410 — seventeen years before his father went into West Park. hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The Barrys stop being a surname in this archive in 1859 and go on being a set of first names for another eighty years. And a sixth, off the 1942 list The Johannesburg cemetery index carries a George Downing Daschner , buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He is not on his father's death notice because he was dead seventeen years before it was written — a twelfth child. George Downing is the name of Kathleen Barry's own grandson, born in 1901, and here it is on an infant in another family in the same decade. A second of the name died in 1998.

hits.text: Indwe. Married. Since 1908. Forty-seven in July 1932 against twenty-two in September 1908 — which makes him forty-six. One year. Brixton Cemetery, 31 July 1932 , where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its Johannesburg dead: Anna J. Mary Booyzen in 1914, John Barry Booyzen in 1916, George Downing Daschner in 1925. And “Sasanna Adriana Booyzen” was buried at Johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him. What does not No parents are named , because a South African civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten.

stephanus-francois-booyzen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. SILVERTON, PRETORIA, a double stone under one base reading BOOYZEN: “'n SIMBOOL VAN LIEFDE — AAN MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT EN ONS VADER — STEFANUS FRANCOIS — ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 — Sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'Heer, dit is Gods wil. Ges. 75:1”. HIS BIRTH IS NOW EXACT: 29 SEPTEMBER 1874, where this archive had only “c. October 1874”. And a pillar between the two halves lists TWELVE CHILDREN by their household names — OUBOET · OUSIE · BESSIE · BETIE · HENNA · EVERT · ✝BABA · FANIE · WILLIE · PIETIE · JOHAN · HENNIE — one of them marked dead with a cross. This archive had almost none of them. They are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. HIS GRAVE IS FOUND AND PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN STEFANUS FRANCOIS 1874-1940”, SILVERTON MAIN CEMETERY, PRETORIA — a joint stone with his wife, “BOOYZEN BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA NEE BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. Both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. He died at East Lynne, Pretoria, and lies at Silverton. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 28 against this archive's c. October 1874, which would have made him 26. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. AND THEN THE PRISONER NUMBER LED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. The medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOYSEN, BURGER, whose PoW number is 18463 — the same number as the register — and it says he was a ZARP, one of the ZAR's police, based at PRETORIA. Quoting a City Coins auction catalogue of November 2020 that described his ABO medal and the papers with it: in action at TALANA, MODDER SPRUIT, COLENSO, PLATRAND (WAGON HILL) where he was WOUNDED IN THE RIGHT LEG ABOVE THE KNEE, SPION KOP and DALMANUTHA — the ZARPs' famous last stand. His applications were completed by his commanding officer, COMMANDANT J. P. DE LA C. SCHROEDER. He was one of FORTY-TWO Boers taken at Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley on 25 April 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to INDIA. This archive has NOT seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. WHAT IT DOES TO THE DISPUTE: he is numbered 18463 and David Schalk Booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at EAST LYNNE, PRETORIA, which is the district all three were taken in. That is a FOURTH point favouring David Schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. It is still not a document naming a parent. PARENTAGE DISPUTED — see below. A son of the second marriage, and a MESSELAAR — a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. His 1940 Sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both parents. Married BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA BOSHOFF at Mosselbaai on 5 SEPTEMBER 1905, certificate 1318 — he 30 and a JONKMAN, she SIXTEEN with her parents consenting. Eleven children; left immovable property and a will. THE REGISTER GIVES HIS RESIDENCE AS PRETORIA, and eleven weeks later David Schalk Booijzen of Goede Hoop, Pretoria — whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called Stephanus François — remarried in that same city. This archive placed him under Petrus Jacobus on his birth year alone. It is marked SERIOUS on the disputed page and it is not decided.

beatrix-magdalena-catharina-boshoff.b: 16 Jun 1889, baptised 16 Feb 1890 at Mossel Bay
beatrix-magdalena-catharina-boshoff.r: HER HALF OF THE SILVERTON STONE READS: “AAN ONS DIERBARE MOEDER — BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA (GEB. BOSHOFF) — ✳ 18-7-1888, † 23-5-1977 — Deur Jesus was vrede behaal, sy kruisdood het alles betaal. Ges. 12:6”. THE DEATH IS NEW AND THE BIRTH DISAGREES WITH THIS ARCHIVE. Her baptism at Mossel Bay on 16 February 1890 gives her born 16 JUNE 1889; the stone says 18 JULY 1888, and the eGGSA index transcribes it 1889. A baptism register written weeks after the event outranks a stone cut eighty-eight years later, so this archive keeps 1889 — and records the disagreement rather than hiding it. BURIED AT SILVERTON, PRETORIA, on a joint stone with her husband: “nee BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. The birth year matches her 1890 Mossel Bay baptism and 1977 is a death year this archive did not have. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. His widow, who signed the 1940 death notice at Pretoria on 26 July 1940 — and who could not name her husband's parents. SHE WAS SIXTEEN when she married him at Mosselbaai on 5 September 1905, with her parents consenting; he was thirty. Her own parents were EVERT PHILIP BOSHOFF and SUSANNA FREDERIKA ALETTA MEYER, named on her 1890 baptism — and two of her eleven children are called straight after them.

hits.text: None of that is a new person. It is the difference between a record and a corroborated record , and it took one search and five photographs. 1940 · The pillar at Silverton — twelve household names, matched to eleven legal ones The centre pillar of the double stone at Silverton lists the children of Stefanus Francois Booyzen and Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Boshoff by the names they were called at home. His 1940 estate lists eleven children by the names they were registered under. The two lists have never been set side by side, and doing it identifies a twelfth child. david-schalk-booyzen-of-1940.r: AND THE ESTATE INDEX AGREES WITH THE STONE, which is what moves him from inferred to documented: “MHG 7653/66 — BOOYZEN, DAVID SCHALK, 1966”. The stone gives an initial and a year; the estate index gives the name in full and the same year. Two collections that do not speak to each other, found an hour apart. OUBOET ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR, and now a grave: “BOOYZEN DAVID S. 1907–1966 & RACHEL M. 1909–1973”, Zandfontein cemetery, Pretoria. The initial, the forename, the town and a birth two years after his parents’ 1905 marriage all agree, and he is the only David S. Booyzen in the Gauteng collection. IT IS A MATCH ON A NAME AND A DATE, NOT A DOCUMENT, and it is marked inferred for that reason. FROM THE INDEX; no image read. Eldest named on his father's 1940 estate — and a name that matters. If Stephanus Francois is DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN's son, as the 1900 death notice suggests, then this boy is called after his grandfather outright. Under the reading this archive published instead, he is called after a great-uncle. It is a point in the argument and not a proof.

hits.text: Matched by position — he heads the estate list. OUSIE Susanna Fredrika Aletta Booyzen Not a name either: ousie , eldest sister. Matched by position — and she is the only daughter left over once the other three are matched by name. BESSIE Elizabeth Magrieta Booyzen Bessie ← Elizabeth BETIE Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Booyzen Betie ← Beatrix — her mother's name entire HENNA Johanna Catharina Booyzen Henna ← Johanna. The weakest of the nine: Henna can also stand for Hendrina, and there is no Hendrina on the estate. EVERT Ewert Philippus Booyzen The same name, spelt as the family said it ✝ BABA Nobody A TWELFTH CHILD. Cut with a birth star and a cross and no name at all — baba is simply baby .

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written. FANIE Stephanus Francois Booyzen the younger Fanie ← Stefanus. Standard, and unambiguous. WILLIE Willem Hendrik Booyzen Willie ← Willem PIETIE Petrus Jacobus Booyzen Pietie ← Petrus JOHAN Johan Abraham Frederik Booyzen The same name HENNIE Hendrik Rudolph Philippus Booyzen Hennie ← Hendrik Eleven names on the estate, twelve on the stone, and every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once. That is what makes the twelfth real. Nine of the matches are ordinary Afrikaans diminutives; two — ouboet and ousie — are not names but places in the family, and they fall to the two children the diminutives leave over.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written. FANIE Stephanus Francois Booyzen the younger Fanie ← Stefanus. Standard, and unambiguous. WILLIE Willem Hendrik Booyzen Willie ← Willem PIETIE Petrus Jacobus Booyzen Pietie ← Petrus JOHAN Johan Abraham Frederik Booyzen The same name HENNIE Hendrik Rudolph Philippus Booyzen Hennie ← Hendrik Eleven names on the estate, twelve on the stone, and every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once. That is what makes the twelfth real. Nine of the matches are ordinary Afrikaans diminutives; two — ouboet and ousie — are not names but places in the family, and they fall to the two children the diminutives leave over. Nothing is left unassigned except ✝ BABA .

baba-booyzen.r: A TWELFTH CHILD, AND THE ONLY WORD CUT FOR HER OR HIM IS “BABA”. The centre pillar of the Silverton stone lists twelve children by their household names; the 1940 estate lists eleven by their registered ones; and when the two are set side by side EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS CLAIMED EXACTLY ONCE, leaving “✝ BABA” — a birth star, a cross, and no name — with nothing to match. Not on the estate because the child was already dead when it was written. NO DATE, NO SEX, NO NAME, NO ORDER beyond the stone's own. This archive has met the shape before: Joseph Heinrich Daschner's 1942 notice named eleven children and the Brixton register produced a twelfth. A death notice lists the living; a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The register → A death notice lists the living. A gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children. That is the difference between the two documents, and it is worth more than either of them alone. What is not claimed. No birth date, no sex, no order of birth beyond the stone's own order, and no name — the child is entered here as Baba Booyzen because that is the only word cut for it. The matches above are readings of nicknames, not documents, and the household page marks every one of them as inferred rather than stated. The mother's own name is on the stone as Betie 's: the family reused it inside one generation. What was searched today and not found Four questions worked properly and answered no , or not yet .

The naming argues for the new reading: her father was STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no Stephanus Francois anywhere in the Pretorius side.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The form did not change. The person filling it in did. Her husband signed it, and her parents were alive and reachable. Withdrawn — Maggie born 1 October 1926 · Taken back This archive carried Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth “Maggie” Booyzen’s birth as 1 October 1926, taken from the family tree. Her mother’s 1944 death notice, written and signed by her father three months before he lost her, gives 14 October 1926. Every other child’s date on that list matches what the archive already held, which is what makes the one mismatch worth taking seriously. Corrected to 14 October.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house. In 1840 a relative of James Montjoy filled in the same printed form at the same box. He knew the dead man's trade, his house, what it was worth, the village he died in and the name of his wife's first husband. Where it asked for the parents, he wrote: "Names of the Parents of the Deceased. Not Known ." — and for birth-place, only "Europe" . James Montjoy had died thirteen years earlier .

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So of the three figures the archive had, the marriage register is the outlier : it gives his age as 22 in December 1879, when he was 28 . His 1905 death registration says 55 , which is right within a year. The 1879 entry is wrong by six years. And he was named for his godfather The witnesses are Willem Hermanus Pieterzen , Maria Catharina Magdalena Potgieter and Xaverius Hermanus Pieterzen . (The archive scan corrects this archive's earlier reading of the surname as Pietersen — see below; the first given name, earlier read as Iwerus , is still not certain.) Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's half-brothers were Pieterzens — the sons of Anna Catharina Sleer by her first marriage.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: A third indexing, under the spelling Montyoy , did. Graaff-Reinet marriage register, folios 60–61. "Den 9 Maart 1817 getrouwd" — married on 9 March 1817. The entry, with a pencil cross beside it: "James Montjoy — Met · Anna Catharina Slier, weduwe van Harmanus Pieterze[n]" What it does not say, and that is the point This archive went to this register expecting an origin . Cape marriage entries of this date routinely record where a party came from, and this very page does it repeatedly — three couples in the right-hand column are entered "beide van Uitenhage" . Against James Montjoy's name there is a long ruled dash and nothing else .

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: Willem Hermanus “Willy” Booyzen 1925–1996 Eldest of the Johannesburg family. William Herman Daschner b. c. 1915 And out through a daughter into a third surname. This archive published “Willem Hermanus is a Booyzen name” and withdrew it. Three documents name the first husband three ways — Harmanus Pieterze in 1817, William Pietersen in 1840, Willem Hermanus Pieterzen in 1851 — and the man they name married into the line and died before it started. Five generations of women, across four surnames — and it is not a Barry name Catherine Maria Sophia This archive called it “a Barry name that outlives the Barry surname by eighty years”.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: One of them was accumulating and one of them was not. The line → 1902 · A wrong name in the index, and a right family behind it Searching the Cape probate index for Hercules Johannes Mountjoy returns exactly one hit. It is not his. Kennisgeving van Sterfgeval , filed 3 January 1903. Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta van Niekerk, geboren Botha , died at her own house at Dordrecht , 18 December 1902. Why it comes up Because his name is written on it. Fifth in her list of eleven children: "5. Maria Sophia van Niekerk, getrouwd met Hercules Johannes Mountjoy." The FamilySearch index keys every name on the page , so a search hit is not a statement about whose document it is.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So the van Niekerks are now documented. Maria Sophia van Niekerk , who married Hercules Johannes Mountjoy at Dordrecht on 8 October 1888, was a daughter of Jan Dirk Abram Frans van Niekerk and Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta Botha , who was herself born in the district of Cradock and whose parents were Philip Rudolph Botha and a mother of the same long name. Her ten brothers and sisters were Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta, Cornelius, Maria Francina Cecilia (widow of Gert Olivier), Jan Dirk Abram Frans, Hercules Johannes , Christiaan Jacobus, Cornelia Elizabeth Gertruida (married James Ross), Benjamin Jacobus, Pieter Jacobus and Philip Rudolph.

hits.text: William Herman Daschner , who was a name on his father's 1942 notice and nothing else, is MHG 2703/63 in the estate index and “DASCHNER Willie 1915–1963” on a West Park stone. The index gives the registered name and the year; the stone gives the household name and the same year. Fritz Johannes Mountjoy , baptised at Barkly East in 1894, lies in Barkly East main cemetery, 1893–1973. Neither was found by looking for him. Both fell out of sweeping a surname. A method note, because it cost an hour. NAAIRS treats two keywords as OR unless the operator between them is sent explicitly. BARRY with BURGERSDORP returned 6,245 documents — more than BARRY alone — and looked for a moment like a rich seam.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months. On 8 November 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married Hendrik Stefanus Palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still. Replacement naming is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart.

john-barry.r: One profile holding two men — and on 14 September 2026 they came apart. THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

Her own DEATH NOTICE 1291, filed by her son R. P. Barry at Barkly East in May 1915, THREE YEARS after she died, gives her age as 84, her nationality as AFRIKANDER OF EUROPEAN EXTRACTION, her father as “Kolbe, thinks James was Christian name” and her mother as UNKNOWN. She died in R. P. Barry’s house at Manorowen and left NOTHING — no movable property, no immovable, estate Nil, no will. And she names NINE children where her husband’s notice names eight. The ninth is WILLIAM.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: The Schoemans sit alongside the Barrys in the same way. P. Schoeman witnessed the 1879 Booysen–Barry marriage ; Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann married Hendrik Nicholaas Barry in 1877; and the 1901 Pretorius–Barry wedding was held at the home of D. Schoeman . Why that matters → The names give it away Anna's mother was christened Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry — the same four names, in the same order, as her own grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . And Anna herself was "named after Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann" , her father's mother, a fact the tree records explicitly rather than leaving to be inferred.

james-henry-barry.v: Henry Jaonas Barry · Hennery James Berry (both 1848 index entries)
james-henry-barry.r: SETTLED, 14 September 2026, and it removes a candidate rather than adding one. The HENRY JAONAS BARRY who turned up on 13 September — “baptised at twenty years old” in 1868, and briefly a candidate for a tenth child — IS THIS MAN. The same event is indexed twice: once as Henry Jaonas Barry, baptism 13 Nov 1868, and once as HENNERY JAMES BERRY, baptism 13 Nov 1848. Same birth date of 13 July 1848, same parents, same collection, and FamilySearch attaches BOTH to one tree person, James Henry Barry 1848–1939. The volume decides the year on its own: the register is “GRAAFF-REINET. BAPTISM RECORDS 1846–1851”, and a baptism of 1868 cannot sit in a book that closes in 1851. So he was baptised at four months, not at twenty, AT GRAAFF-REINET — not at Cape Town or Tulbagh, which is what both index entries say for the place. The birth-spacing argument made against him held: his brother John Augustus II was born 13 March 1847 and he was born sixteen months later. THE IMAGE HAS BEEN LOCATED AND NOT READ — identifier apid:TH-909-70517-31299-17. Named on the 1915 death notice, which he swore himself. The index now dates him: born about 1847, dead at Barkly East on 23 June 1939, having outlived his father by thirty-six years. BUT THAT YEAR CANNOT STAND. His brother John Augustus Barry II was born 13 MARCH 1847 off a register, and “about 1847” here is not a date at all — it is an age worked back from the 1939 death. Two brothers cannot share it. A relationship search on his mother's surname turned up a HENRY JAONAS BARRY born 13 July 1848 and baptised at twenty, which is where a next child belongs; whether that is this man under a clerk's ear is UNPROVED and the register is unread.

hits.text: The reasoning below is left standing because the archive argued itself to the right answer before the record confirmed it. HENRY JAONAS BARRY IS JAMES HENRY BARRY. The same baptism is indexed twice. One entry reads Henry Jaonas Barry, baptism 13 Nov 1868 ; the other reads Hennery James Berry, baptism 13 Nov 1848 . Both give the birth as 13 July 1848 , both name John Barry and Margret Willemina Kolbe , both sit in the Cape Town Archives DRC collection, and FamilySearch attaches both to one tree person — James Henry Barry, 1848–1939 , which is this archive's man, dead at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. The volume settles the year without the image being read.

It may not be a new child: this archive holds a James Henry Barry , born about 1847, who died at Barkly East on 23 June 1939.

It also names his father as John Barry and his mother's maiden name as "Neagle" — almost certainly Nagle , of County Cork. The note's own conclusion is a question: if he was born on the high seas with the 1820 Settlers , who were his parents? The 1820 Settler hypothesis does not survive arithmetic.

Margaret Wilhelmina Elizabeth is the Barry name that runs down the other side of this family too. William Herman is Willem Hermanus , her father. Richard Peter is her uncle, Richard Peter Barry . Henry James is her brother. Five of eleven Daschner children carry Booyzen and Barry names. The surname leaves the family in one generation. The names do not. This is the same evidence the archive uses on the name and in the cousin marriage : in this family, forenames are inherited property, and they travel through daughters as reliably as surnames travel through sons.

richard-pieter-kolbe-barry.r: AND THE NAME IS IN A GOVERNMENT FILE, TWICE OVER, IN ONE LINE. SAB, VWR volume 2, reference B645/8/38, 1937: “AANSOEK DEUR PLAASEIENAAR BARKLY-OOS. RPK BARRY. BYWONER RPK BARRY (SEUN).” An application by a farm owner at Barkly East — R.P.K. BARRY — and the bywoner on the place is R.P.K. BARRY, HIS SON. TWO MEN OF THESE INITIALS AT BARKLY EAST IN 1937, one holding the land and one working it as a tenant, and the state file is between them. This archive cannot say which of the two is the man born in 1899 and does not guess. A BYWONER is not a labourer and not an owner; it is the word South Africa used in the 1930s for a white tenant farming another man's ground, and VWR is the Department of Social Welfare. THE FILE HAS NOT BEEN READ. CARRIES BOTH NAMES AT ONCE — Richard Pieter, for the Barry of Manorowen, and Kolbe, for the 1820 Settler family his great-grandmother married out of. Married Maria Magdalena Siebert. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.

william-henry-keys.r: Married JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY, baptised at Burgersdorp on 29 February 1860 — a daughter of George Mountjoy and Maria Sophia Botha, which this archive had been asking about and can now answer. Eight children baptised across Dordrecht, Barkly East and Barkly West between 1878 and 1898: Robert Byron, William Henry, JAMES JONATHAN, George, Lancelott Byron, Cecil Frederik, Rachel Anna Maria and HERKLAAS EDWARD JOHANNES. The Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname, exactly as the Barry names crossed into the Daschners — and BYRON twice, which appears nowhere else in this archive.

johanna-catharina-mountjoy-of-burgersdor.r: A daughter of George Mountjoy and Maria Sophia Botha, baptised on a LEAP DAY, and the woman who married William Henry Keys. This archive has carried “a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy” married to Keys since the index was read and could not say which one. This one.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The claim Where it stands The family were Cape Rebels Yes — but under the other surname Of the 26 Booysens on the roll not one is from this district, and Booyzen returns nothing at all . The surname BARRY had never been searched. It returns four, and two are here: Fred J. Barry of Ivanhoe, Barkly East / Wodehouse, tried June 1901 — the same month as Daniel Willem Schoeman of Caerlaverock , in whose house the family married five weeks later — and Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint , which is Kathleen Barry's brother's name. Identity unproven; the district is not. The rebels → The spelling was changed to avoid the "joiners" The change is on paper. The spelling was not new.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: A second of the name died in 1998. This comes from an index and not from an image, and the page says so. But it moves the reading: six names, not five , and a pattern that cannot comfortably be called coincidence. The namesakes → This matters to the rebel question in a small, real way. When the Cape Rebel roll produces a Fred J. Barry of Ivanhoe and a Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint, the second name is not a coincidence to be waved at — it is a name this family demonstrably used and kept using. It still does not prove the man on the roll is Kathleen's brother, and this archive still marks that unproven . But it does mean the name is evidence of a family, not of an individual.

henry-james-kolbe-barry.r: NEW, AND HE CARRIES THE WHOLE ARGUMENT IN HIS NAME. “BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE. BORN IN BARKLY EAST, CAPE PROVINCE. UNMARRIED. DECEASED ESTATE”, Pietermaritzburg Archives Repository, MSCE 2183/1958. HENRY JAMES is the Barry forename this archive has followed since 1848; KOLBE is the surname it has spent the project proving is the source of half the family's given names. HERE THEY ARE IN ONE MAN, born in this archive's own town, dying UNMARRIED in Natal in 1958 — so the names stop with him. He is the third Barry found carrying Kolbe as a forename, after Richard Pieter Kolbe Barry and Anton Rector Kolbe Barry. NO PARENTS NAMED; the estate is not read.

hits.title: What has been searched
hits.text: BARRY + BARKLY (all repositories) 2 documents Partly SAB VWR B645/8/38 (1937): an application by a FARM OWNER AT BARKLY-OOS, R.P.K. BARRY, with his son of the same initials as bywoner. Given this family's Barry–Kolbe naming — Henry James Kolbe Barry, Anthon Rector Kolbe Barry — R.P.K. is very likely Richard Peter Kolbe Barry. That ties the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, the R. P. Barry who signed the 1915 notice at Manorowen, and five mortgage bonds of 1895–1903 into one landholding man at Barkly East. Tighter, still not proof.

catherine-mary-sophia-barry-of-1855.r: THE TENTH CHILD, FOUND BY READING 267 REGISTER IMAGES — and she has the same name as her sister. Burgersdorp doopregister, image group 008039088, image 427: born 10 JULY 1855, baptised 22 JULY 1855, father JOHN BARRY, mother MARGARET LOUISA KOLBE. FOUR YEARS LATER THE SAME PARENTS BAPTISED ANOTHER CATHARINA MARY SOPHIA at Dordrecht, born 4 August 1859 — the woman who married into the Booyzens and carried the name to Australia. TWO DAUGHTERS, ONE NAME, DIFFERENT BIRTHDAYS FOUR YEARS APART IN DIFFERENT TOWNS. A baptism is not done twice, so the ordinary reading is the ordinary Cape practice: THIS CHILD DIED, AND THE NAME WAS GIVEN AGAIN. This archive has no burial for her and states the death only as “before August 1859”. AND SHE EXPLAINS THE NAME TWICE OVER: the archive has already shown CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA is a Kolbe name, off the 1848 godmother Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber. It was thought important enough to use, lose, and use again.

a-werdmuller-child-of-1857.r: AND BY THE AFTERNOON THERE WAS A CANDIDATE FOR THE MISSING NAME. The Queenstown Free Press of 13 February 1884 marries “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER, OF STEYNSBURG, SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER, OF BURGHERSDORP” to Charlotte Anne Callaghan. A man born 14 February 1857 was twenty-seven that week. NOT PROVED: no document read here names Charles Andrew’s mother, and his father — or a man of exactly that name — married again at Burgersdorp in 1874. NAMELESS IN THE INDEX, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The same sweep that found the tenth Barry child turned up a second entry with an EMPTY NAME COLUMN: born 14 February 1857, baptised 10 April 1857 at Burgersdorp, mother AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, father COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER. She is the Settler's fourth daughter, born at Graaff-Reinet in 1829 — and this is the first of her children this archive has ever seen. THE CHILD'S OWN NAME IS ON THE PAGE AND NOT IN THE INDEX, so no search will ever return it. The register image has not been read; only the index line.

g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.v: almost certainly GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the Settler's twin son
g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.r: A DATE FOR THE TWIN, IF IT IS HIM. The stone at PIET RETIEF reads “VADER EN MOEDER — G.A. KOLBE — GEB. 23 FEB. 1836 — OVERL. 7 JAN. 1913 — A.M. KOLBE — GEB. 4 MEI 1843 — OVERL. 21 SEP. 1907 — VAN HUN KINDERS”. The Settler's ninth and tenth children were TWINS born at BURGERSDORP IN 1836, Charlotte Felicia and George Augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. A G.A. KOLBE BORN 23 FEBRUARY 1836 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT MAN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT YEAR — and it would date his twin sister too. IT IS INITIALS AND A YEAR, NOT A NAME AND A PARENT, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. It would also give the OTHER George Augustus Kolbe — born Burgersdorp 2 October 1861, dead Standerton 1934, buried Wakkerstroom — a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern Transvaal Kolbes have been missing.

john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary.

anna-jacoba-van-der-merwe.r: SHE REMARRIED, AND HER SECOND HUSBAND IS WHY SHE WAS HARD TO FIND. The Free State archives hold her under a different surname: VAB MHG M777 — “MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA. NOOIENSVAN VAN DER MERWE. EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON [KOLBE]”, 1896. WIDOWED IN 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN AND DEAD TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER AS MRS MCCABE. Her husband’s own estate is beside it — VAB MHG K71, “KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. EGGENOTE ANNA JACOBA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1868. AND THE McCABE NAME IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE: a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE was baptised at Bloemfontein in 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA MCCABE — a second Kolbe–McCabe marriage in the same small Free State world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. NEITHER ESTATE IS READ. M777 is the document that would name the twelve children. Married JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE on 3 APRIL 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. She is the third van der Merwe to marry into these families.

coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.r: HE IS IN THE CAPE ARCHIVES FROM 1854 TO 1882 AND HE DIED IN 1882, not merely “before February 1884”. Motions in the Supreme Court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men’s insolvent estates; and in 1882, GSC 2/1/1/41 no. 60, “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER AND COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER TRADING AS C.A. WERDMULLER AND COMPANY” — FATHER AND SON IN BUSINESS TOGETHER, in the year he died. His own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. THE MAN THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER MARRIED, and until today a bracket after her name. He is at BURGERSDORP in April 1857, standing at a font with AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE. He is at Burgersdorp again on 7 JULY 1874, married BY SPECIAL LICENCE by the Rev. William Cromar to ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER — and the Eastern Province Herald prints his name in full as COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D’ELGG, which is the first time this archive has seen the von Elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. He is DEAD by February 1884, when his second son marries as the son of “the late C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp”. WHETHER AUGUSTA LOUISA WAS DEAD BEFORE 1874 THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW.

charles-andrew-werdmuller.r: THE DATES NOW CLOSE AROUND HIM, THOUGH NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES HIS MOTHER. His father’s first wife, AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, MADE A WILL IN 1868 AND DIED IN 1873 — KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG”, filed 1873 — and his father remarried on 7 JULY 1874. IN 1882 CHARLES ANDREW WAS IN BUSINESS WITH HIS FATHER as C.A. Werdmuller and Company, and in February 1884 he married. A SON OF THE 1874 MARRIAGE WOULD HAVE BEEN SEVEN AND NINE. He can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the Settler’s daughter. THE ONE LOOPHOLE LEFT is an earlier wife before Augusta Louisa, and his father’s 1882 DEATH NOTICE would close it by naming the children. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER OF BURGHERSDORP, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, on 13 FEBRUARY 1884 to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan of Ashby Manor. Of STEYNSBURG then, and by 1909 CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P., OF HOOPSTAD in the Orange River Colony — the town his wife died in. HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON ANYTHING READ HERE. If he is the child born 14 February 1857 at Burgersdorp he is AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE’S SON and a grandson of the 1820 Settler; if he belongs to his father’s 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. THE DATES FAVOUR KOLBE AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY IT.

augusta-louisa-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS THREE DOCUMENTS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NONE OF THEM. A WILL, MADE IN 1868 AND FILED IN 1873: KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA. WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG” — which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. A DEATH NOTICE, MOOC 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. And a LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, MOOC 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. SHE DIED IN 1873 AND HER HUSBAND REMARRIED IN JULY 1874 — a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son Charles Andrew is. NONE OF THE THREE IS READ.
